lines.text: Do your nerve cells touch? Mostly, no. For decades, no microscope could show it.
lines.phonemes: dˈuː jɔː nˈɜːv sˈɛlz tˈʌtʃ? mˈəʊstli, nˈəʊ. fɔː dˈɛkeɪdz, nˈəʊ mˈaɪkɹəskˌəʊp kʊd ʃˈəʊ ɪt.

lines.text: Your brain holds over a hundred trillion meeting points: over ten thousand for every person alive. Through a lens, they look joined.
lines.phonemes: jɔː bɹˈeɪn hˈəʊldz ˌəʊvəɹ ɐ hˈʌndɹɪd tɹˈɪliən mˈiːtɪŋ pˈɔɪnts: ˌəʊvə tˈɛn θˈaʊzənd fɔːɹ ˈɛvɹɪ pˈɜːsən ɐlˈaɪv. θɹuː ɐ lˈɛnz, ðeɪ lˈʊk dʒˈɔɪnd.

lines.text: Camillo Golgi, who made the stain, saw one continuous web. With it, Santiago Ramón y Cajal saw separate cells. In nineteen oh six they shared a Nobel, still arguing.
lines.phonemes: kamˈɪləʊ ɡˈɒldʒi , hˌuː mˌeɪd ðə stˈeɪn, sˈɔː wˈɒn kəntˈɪnjuːəs wˈɛb. wɪð ɪt, sˌantɪˈɑːɡəʊ ɹamˈɒn i kəhˈɑːl sˈɔː sˈɛpɹət sˈɛlz. ɪn nˈaɪntiːn ˈəʊ sˈɪks ðeɪ ʃˈeəd ɐ nəʊbˈɛl, stˈɪl ˈɑːɡjuːɪŋ.

lines.text: In the nineteen fifties, electron microscopes finally showed it: a gap. At most junctions, electricity can't jump it. Calcium floods the tip, tiny sacs spill a chemical messenger, and it drifts across.
lines.phonemes: ɪnðə nˈaɪntiːn fˈɪftiz, ɪlˈɛktɹɒn mˈaɪkɹəskˌəʊps fˈaɪnəli ʃˈəʊd ɪt: ɐ ɡˈap. at mˈəʊst dʒˈʌŋkʃənz, ɪlɛktɹˈɪsɪti kˈɑːnt dʒˈʌmp ɪt. kˈalsiəm flˈʌdz ðə tˈɪp, tˈaɪni sˈaks spˈɪl ɐ kˈɛmɪkəl mˈɛsɪndʒə, and ɪt dɹˈɪfts əkɹˈɒs.

lines.text: The handoff takes about a thousandth of a second. Use a junction, and it can grow stronger: likely part of how you learn.
lines.phonemes: ðə hˈandɒf tˈeɪks ɐbˌaʊt ɐ θˈaʊzəndθ əvə sˈɛkənd. jˈuːs ɐ dʒˈʌŋkʃən, and ɪt kan ɡɹˈəʊ stɹˈɒŋɡə: lˈaɪkli pˈɑːt ɒv hˌaʊ juː lˈɜːn.

lines.text: So your nerve cells mostly don't touch. They talk, across gaps, in chemicals.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ jɔː nˈɜːv sˈɛlz mˈəʊstli dˈəʊnt tˈʌtʃ. ðeɪ tˈɔːk, əkɹˌɒs ɡˈaps, ɪn kˈɛmɪkəlz.

lines.text: Meanwhile, as you watched, you took about fifteen breaths. Each started at the base of your brain and crossed gaps like these.
lines.phonemes: mˈiːnwaɪl, az juː wˈɒtʃt, juː tˈʊk ɐbˌaʊt fˈɪftiːn bɹˈɛθs. ˈiːtʃ stˈɑːtɪd at ðə bˈeɪs ɒv jɔː bɹˈeɪn and kɹˈɒst ɡˈaps lˈaɪk ðˈiːz.

lines.text: Next: those breaths. Where does all that air go?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: ðəʊz bɹˈɛθs. wˌeə dˈʌz ˈɔːl ðat ˈeə ɡˈəʊ?
